text: This is ARMOR, the Advanced Rider Monitoring and Orientation Reasoning System. It watches over your riding group, and calls for help when you can't. Let's walk through every screen and every button.

The home screen shows what's ready: location, S M S, and emergency contacts. Finish setting up opens a one time checklist: location all the time, S M S, calls, notifications, microphone, battery, and full screen alarms, so protection keeps working with the screen off.
In the Group tab, enter your name and phone number. Your number is shared only with the riders in your ride, so they can text and call you if you go down.
Tap create ride. ARMOR makes a six letter code. Invite riders shares the code and a link through WhatsApp or S M S. As the creator, you lead the ride, and can start or end it for everyone.
In Settings, add emergency contacts. Pick from contacts opens your phone's own contacts app. You can also type a number in any format, and it's saved in international form.

Each contact has a call button, which rings them straight away through your phone app, and a message button, which opens your messages app. Send test S O S text checks that texting works on your phone.

Settings also covers always-on protection, calling after an S O S, the hands-free voice option, the emergency number, and your medical I D: blood group, allergies, conditions and medications, which are texted with an S O S.
Slide to ride. ARMOR starts tracking on a live street map. Kabir has joined with the code, and appears on the map. The status shows you're with the group.
The map has five views: map, night, terrain, satellite, and hybrid. Drag to move, pinch or use the buttons to zoom, and tap recentre to follow the group again.
Drag the panel down for a full screen map, with your status and the S O S button still in reach. Drag it up to bring back your stats and controls.
Chat opens the group conversation. Quick replies send with one tap, or type a message. Kabir's reply arrives in moments. Back closes the chat.
Need a hand asks the group for non-emergency help, like a puncture or fuel. When someone responds, you see who's coming. Tap again to cancel.
Open riders, lead and safety tools. As the lead, team stop asks everyone to stop, with a reason. Riders confirm, and ride on releases the group. Just me marks only you as stopped.

Report hazard marks a pothole, oil, an accident, animals, police, or roadwork for the riders behind. Off the bike pauses crash detection while you walk around. Regroup here sets a meeting point. Quick status buttons tell the group you're stopped for fuel, a break, or a repair.

Tap the mic, or press your helmet button, then speak: stop for fuel, status, read messages, call Mom, or pothole ahead. ARMOR answers out loud. This emulator has no microphone, so it hears nothing here.
The log tab keeps a record of everything that happened on the ride, from stops and alerts to messages and S O S events.

Now the S O S. Hold the red button for one and a half seconds. ARMOR texts your location and medical details to every emergency contact and every rider, then calls them one by one, nearest rider first, all on its own. I'm okay cancels it, and everyone is told it was a false alarm.
If you stop away from the group and don't respond, ARMOR asks if you're okay. Then it alerts the group, and if nobody answers, it sends the S O S automatically. One tap on I'm okay cancels.
End the ride from the panel. ARMOR asks to confirm, then shows your ride summary: distance, time, moving time and speeds.
ARMOR. Ride together. Come home together.
